findings.text: She had been born in a forest and had never thought of a wood as a bad place to be. She thought it now: both sides of the road and a roof over it, and four horses in a line down the middle making all the noise in the world.
findings.deletionTest: Cutting the 'had never thought' half leaves 'She thought it now: both sides of the road...' which needs the negated antecedent, so the sentence has to be recast affirmatively. The facts (forest-born, the wood is bad tonight, the reasons) all survive the recast.
findings.reason: 'had never thought X. She thought it now' is the 'It should not have helped. It did.' reversal shape. The narrator sets up the old belief so the new one can land, rather than Sylvanas arguing with herself, so condition 4 does not apply.
findings.suggestedFix: She had been born in a forest, and tonight this wood was a bad place to be: both sides of the road and a roof over it, and four horses in a line down the middle making all the noise in the world.

findings.text: There had not been a name in any of this.
findings.deletionTest: Read from the positive: 'A name. ... And now a house with a lord in it, a seat at court, a seal...' It survives. The lead sentence only frames the run of nameless items (said nothing / nobody could keep hold of / no name) that builds toward the noun.
findings.reason: Pattern 7. A negated frame opens a chain of refusals that leads to one noun (the name). The recap items under it are concrete facts and can stay. The frame sentence carries no fact of its own.
findings.suggestedFix: Every name so far had been a place.
findings.note: Replace only the frame sentence. The recap items that follow it (boy in a loft, young man with a cart, *Own cart*) keep their factual negations.

audits.auditNote: There are many KEEPs because, after two revision rounds, most of the remaining negations are binary diagnostics in Jaina's readings (light/nothing, light/heavy, source/first), hard constraints (elves cannot feel the contamination, the books carry no carters' names), or Sylvanas's self-argument with an explicit undercut (overseer's stove, old carter). Each KEEP was re-run through self-check questions 1-5, and the full reasoning is in the scratchpad.

audits.cleanReason: First sweep plus the dedicated P5/P6 second sweep over all 696 lines. No infrastructure gets intention verbs: road, causeway, river and hedge verbs are directional or literal ('ran', 'went up', 'held nothing', 'fell back'). Spell-light and contamination behaviour ('The light leaned. It crowded to one side', 'the boards have it', 'one of them sick from end to end') is the in-world mechanism, kept under the subject-matter defense. Document verbs ('The slips said both roads', 'The square of sacking ... said Andorhal') are literal reading of text. Every body-part subject is involuntary or reflexive (knees set, teeth chattering, ears went red, clerk's head coming round to a draught, eyes came open on waking, overseer's hands pressed flat so they would not shake). There are no P9 nominalizations ('realization', 'decision', 'understanding' all absent) and no P11 permission tags (every 'let' is physical, with an animal or person object: 'let the mare have it', 'Sylvanas let Lyriel take him'). There are no P10 receiver-noun revisions: 'Millhaven went on the north road' and 'The fan kept widening' are placements or geometry, and the actor is named in the sentence before. Borderline idioms ('word didn't need a cob to carry it', 'the clock was running', 'every one pointing down this road') each have their human agents named within two paragraphs and carry no intention verb. No infrastructure noun is smeared more than once. PATTERN 4 ALERT: no.
audits.secondSweep: P5/P6 targeted re-read done: (a) roads/geography with motion or fire verbs - all spatial or literal, none intentional; (b) maps/answers/rooms with revision or cognition verbs plus an instrument-phrase demotion - none ('a line ... that sat differently on the page' is followed at once by the concrete hand difference, the smaller crooked writing); (c) body-part volition - none outside reflex; (d) abstract states settling into body parts - none ('she could feel every one of them in her eyes' is literal sleeplessness); (e) metaphor chains on one inanimate subject - none.
